items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: 9 named lines accounted for in the ledger: FR-01.02 #4/#15 (merged, enforced), #5, #8/#8b split, #10/#10b split, #11; FR-01.16 C, #3/#3b split, #6 -- every downgrade (#8b, #10b, #3b) is drift-tested, none gated.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: After 7 external-review rounds every manifest read path (parse failure, non-list/non-object splits, unsafe/absolute/traversal split names, unreadable/missing spec.md, corrupt scope field) fails loud with an explicit CheckResult instead of crashing or silently passing.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: Path-traversal and Windows drive/root-relative split names rejected before any filesystem join (_is_safe_split_name); read-only over project-local files; no secrets, no exec/network sinks.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 67 tests, each asserting the specific failing row/path/reason; includes an empirical round-trip probe against the real producer's bold-anchor + checkbox acceptance-criteria shape, not just the heading-style shape used elsewhere in the fixtures.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: Noted non-blocking inefficiency (GLM round 6): _read_spec_texts runs once per gate (3x per project_checks run) instead of being cached across the 4 gates -- O(splits) file reads, negligible at realistic split counts, not fixed this round.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Pure/wiring split mirrors the established plan_gate_extras.py/design_gate_extras.py pattern; _project_gate_wiring.py stayed at 298 LOC (under the 300 guideline) via a shared _read_project_scope helper extracted round 5.

items.name: Affected Boundaries (ADR-024)
items.note: Boundary: spec.md's FR table as written by the real /shipwright-project producer (spec-generation.md: Area column, bold **FR-XX.YY: Name** anchors, - [ ] checkbox bullets -- different from every other fixture in this diff). Ran a live round-trip probe in the exact real-producer shape with a planted file-path violation; all three spec-text gates fired correctly. Pinned as a permanent regression test. Asymptote reached in one probe -- the question (does fr_criteria support this anchor style) had a single deterministic answer.
